_: PART 29 (P5 — INCOMPLETE-VS-VIOLATION DOMINANCE) ratchet. `known` waives (engine, gate) pairs that are
known-broken, so a real regression elsewhere still fails the suite. IT RATCHETS BOTH WAYS: a waiver whose
cells now all pass ALSO fails it, so deleting the entry is part of the fix.
`known` IS EMPTY, AND IT GOT THERE THE HARD WAY. An extension of this property to a ROUTE x TRIGGER
matrix put 8 cells red across all four engines and they were waived as engine defects. Reading the
clauses afterwards, ALL EIGHT WERE THE PROPERTY BEING STRICTER THAN THE CONTRACT:
· `count0` — SPEC §2 ⟨0.24⟩ binds the count-0 rule to `gate --report` AS A DISCLOSURE, NOT AS AN EXIT
CODE: 'the exit code and the verdict document are UNCHANGED', and 'refusing with exit 2 is not an
available reading'. The clause even records that it first said the opposite and was corrected. All
four engines were right.
· `malformed` — an unreadable SIGNATURE key (`unanalyzed` is named as one) impeaches the DOCUMENT:
'One unreadable among them means the document's claim cannot be trusted … Refuse.' The violation this
property wanted to see dominate is read FROM the impeached document, and §3.3.1's dominance rule is
about incompletely-analyzed CODE, where the violation is the engine's own finding. rust/ts/swift emit
the §3.1 refusal shape and are right.
WHAT SURVIVES THE EXTENSION: `report/declared` — a well-formed ⟨0.21⟩ manifest declaring unanalyzed
source — which is the genuine §3.3.1 case on this route, and all four engines are clean on it.
ONE REAL FINDING CAME OUT OF IT and is filed with the corrupt-report PART rather than waived here: java
does NOT refuse over a malformed `unanalyzed` (it exits 0 when there is nothing else to report), which
the signature-key rule forbids.
THE STANDING HAZARD, twice in one file: a property whose expectation is stricter than the contract
produces findings shaped EXACTLY like real defects, and waiving them records engines as broken for
conforming. Check which side the contract is on before blaming an engine.
